newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent closes higher on Oct NYMEX crude expiry.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent closes higher on Oct NYMEX crude expiry.

text.p: IPE Brent crude futures made a last-minute recovery to end in positive territory on Friday, buoyed by a firm expiry of NYMEX October crude, but overall the the day's action was muted, brokers said.
November Brent closed seven cents higher at $21.98 per barrel, having touched a low of $21.76 during the day.
Just before the Oct NYMEX crude expiry, the Oct/Nov spread jumped 10 cents to +55 cents and November Brent bit the day's high at $22.07 per barrel.
"There was a bit of shortcovering on October NYMEX into the expiry, but it was a thin day," a broker said.
Brokers said the oil complex was held back for the past two days by weak gasoline futures in New York.
"The only thing which is ringing any alarm bells is gasoline which continues to be unsupported and unwanted. It's beginning to put a bit of pressure on heat," a futures broker said.

NYMEX gasoline, which tumbled almost two cents per gallon on Thursday, closed 0.22 cents lower at 61.10 cents. London dealers said movement of gasoline from Europe into the U.S. market was one factor depressing the contract.
The broker said that if gasoline continued to be under pressure and heating oil went below a $66-$66.30 trendline, there was the chance of a further downside.
IPE gas oil futures closed earlier $1.50 a tonne lower at $213.75 a tonne, reversing a rally earlier this week on perceptions of tight supplies on both sides of the Atlantic.
